narr: A frontal boundary remained parked over the Central Appalachians on the last week of July, which kept southwest Virginia suseptible to heavy downpours from daily showers and thunderstorms for a prolonged period of time. Copious amounts of late evening rain on the 27th resulted in nighttime flash flooding in Dickenson County, where pockets of 2 to 4 inches fell. Local creeks and streams rose out of their banks early in the morning of July 28th and resulted in water on roadways and washing out several residential bridges north of Clintwood. High water also entered into the Clintwood Public Library overnight and flooded the first floor of the building.
ev: Water entered into the Clintwood Public Library and permeated on the first floor. Flooding was also observed along Dickenson Highway and Coeburn Road.

Several small residential bridges were washed out north of Clintwood. Brush Creek rose out of its banks and spilled onto Brush Creek Road. Bear Pen Creek also rose out of its banks, flooding to adjacent roadway and the nearby park.
Dickenson Highway was flooded in several spots between Clintwood and Clinchco, closing the road for a brief period of time.
Little Garden Creek rose out of its banks and flooded Little Garden Creek Road.
